claims: TSA PreCheck Touchless ID is an optional biometric program using facial recognition to verify identity at security.
TSA PreCheck Touchless ID eliminates the need to show a physical ID or boarding pass.
TSA PreCheck Touchless ID is available for PreCheck members at over 65 U.S. airports.
TSA PreCheck Touchless ID requires opting in via a participating airline app.
TSA PreCheck Touchless ID requires having a passport on file.
In TSA PreCheck Touchless ID, upon approaching the TSA checkpoint, a camera scans the user's face, comparing it to the user's passport photo.
To enroll in TSA PreCheck Touchless ID, add Known Traveler Number (KTN) and save passport information in airline profile via app or website.
TSA PreCheck Touchless ID requires explicitly opting in to Touchless ID or Biometrics in airline account settings.
Participating airlines for TSA PreCheck Touchless ID include American, Delta, United, Alaska, and others.
A mobile boarding pass for TSA PreCheck Touchless ID shows the 'Touchless ID' indicator, usually a green human icon.
Travel And Tour World says photos in TSA PreCheck Touchless ID are generally deleted within 24 hours and not used for surveillance.
Participating major airports for TSA PreCheck Touchless ID include ATL, LAX, ORD, DFW, EWR, JFK, SFO, SEA, and DEN.
A Reddit post on r/unitedairlines states that some users report TSA PreCheck Touchless ID may sometimes be closed or not working.
NerdWallet's analysis notes that TSA PreCheck Touchless ID is only valid for mobile boarding passes and not printed ones.
